source.report_note: Limits are those of the manufacturer's Table 2 (Fluke 33X ClampMeters Calibration Information, printed pp. 8-9), unchanged. The current, inrush and frequency points are driven through a 50-turn coil (calibrator current x 50 = the reading shown); the Uncertainty of a coil point is that of the 5500A/COIL scope lines at the effective current where they cover it, otherwise the calibrator's at the sourced current x 50; the frequency points carry the calibrator's frequency specification. The four ohms limits are looser than the published accuracy of the Specifications (1 % + 5 counts) and are reported as printed.
source.note: Table 2 of the 33X Calibration Information (PN 1618765, Rev. 2, 12/03): "Performance Tests 333, 334, 335" (14 rows, printed p. 8) and "Performance Tests 336, 337 (cont.)" (27 rows, printed p. 9) = 41 rows (AC volts 5, Min/Max 2, DC volts 8, continuity 2, ohms 4, AC amps 9, inrush 2, DC amps 7, frequency 2). The tables have no step numbers and no X / N/A columns: steps are numbered in table order and the number runs on across the two tables (2A-1 .. 2A-14, then 2B-15 .. 2B-41; the ref T2A #n / T2B #n is the printed row); the models of a row are the table it is printed in (p. 8: 333 334 335; p. 9: 336 337) and the tags printed in the rows (333 / 334, 335 / 337 only / 337), so the Table 2 points per model are 333: 11, 334: 13, 335: 13, 336: 20, 337: 27 (12 / 16 / 16 / 23 / 30 with the functional checks). Table 1 (printed p. 5) names a Fluke 5520A (the program drives a Fluke 5522A, 5520A or 5560A, or you set the calibrator by hand), any Fluke DMM and the Fluke 5500A/Coil (50 turns). The "5520A Output" column of the amps rows lists the current the jaw sees; the calibrator drives that / 50 through the coil (the meter reads 50 x the calibrator current; an inference, as for every clamp meter), the inrush rows (5 A at 60 Hz) and the frequency rows (5 A at 10 Hz, 10 A at 300 Hz) likewise. The meter has no remote interface: you type the display reading. The manual prints one set of limits; they are used as printed. The four ohms limits (590.5 .. 609.5 and 5905 .. 6095) are looser than the printed Specifications (1 % + 5 counts; the limits are 1.5 % + 5 counts) and the 10 Hz frequency limits are the specification rounded outward: both flagged, nothing changed. High-voltage points go straight to the test value (the manual prescribes no ramp). The display, backlight and keypad checks (printed pp. 5-6) are yes / no points that run first (table F: 334-337 three, 333 the keypad only); the calibration ADJUSTMENT (printed pp. 10-12) is not part of this procedure.

COIL_AUX.title: Change the cables: 50-turn coil on the calibrator low-current output
COIL_AUX.summary: Calibrator low-current output (5522A / 5520A AUX HI / AUX LO; 5560A VI AUX / OUTPUT LO) -> 50-turn coil (5500A/COIL) -> the meter jaw closed around the coil. No test leads in the meter jacks.
steps: Meter dial
Turn the meter dial to OFF before you move any lead.
Test leads
REMOVE the test leads from the VΩ and COM jacks while current is measured with the jaw (general practice; the Calibration Information does not say).
Standby
The calibrator is put in STANDBY before you rewire (in manual-calibrator mode, put it in STANDBY yourself).
Coil

The wired coil is 50 turns (Table 1, printed p. 5: Fluke 5500A/Coil; Figure 4, printed p. 7). Connect its two ends to the calibrator low-current output: Fluke 5522A / 5520A AUX HI and AUX LO; Fluke 5560A VI AUX (HI) and OUTPUT LO. Use plugs rated for the current.
Jaw

Close the jaw around the coil (Figure 4 shows the conductor through the jaw), fully closed, the coil centred in the opening, the coil leads kept away from the meter body. The meter then reads 50 x the calibrator current (0.4 A reads 20 A; 0.1 A reads 5 A).
LCOMP

Fluke 5522A / 5520A: the program turns inductive-load compensation (LCOMP) ON for every AC point through the coil (read back with LCOMP?) and OFF afterwards (the Calibration Information, printed p. 7 step 4, asks for LCOMP ON on the 5520A for the amp function; 5522A Operators Manual p. 6-23; on the 5520A the command is UNVERIFIED). Where the calibrator does not allow it (440 Hz and above below 0.33 A; 1 kHz and above from 0.33 A) it is not set and the log says so. 5560A: no LCOMP command for its own output - set it yourself if needed.
Check
Compare your connections with the diagram, then continue.
COIL_AUX.caution: This point drives current through a coil. Keep the calibrator in STANDBY whenever you touch the coil or leads (the manual: "make sure the calibrator is in standby mode (STBY)", printed p. 6).

COIL_20A.title: Change the cables: 50-turn coil on the calibrator high-current output
COIL_20A.summary: Calibrator high-current output (5522A / 5520A 20 A / AUX LO; 5560A 30A / OUTPUT LO) -> 50-turn coil (5500A/COIL) -> the meter jaw closed around the coil. No test leads in the meter jacks.
steps: Meter dial
Turn the meter dial to OFF before you move any lead.
Test leads
REMOVE the test leads from the VΩ and COM jacks while current is measured with the jaw (general practice; the Calibration Information does not say).
Standby
The calibrator is put in STANDBY before you rewire (in manual-calibrator mode, put it in STANDBY yourself).
Coil
Move the two ends of the 50-turn coil to the calibrator high-current terminals: Fluke 5522A / 5520A 20 A and AUX LO; Fluke 5560A 30A and OUTPUT LO. The coil, plugs and leads must carry up to 18 A.
Jaw

The jaw stays closed around the coil (centred, fully closed, leads away from the meter body). The meter reads 50 x the calibrator current: 4 A reads 200 A, 8 A reads 400 A, 12 A reads 600 A, 18 A reads 900 A.
LCOMP
Fluke 5522A / 5520A: AC points through the coil - the program turns LCOMP ON for each (and OFF afterwards), as for the low-current points.
Check
Compare your connections with the diagram, then continue.
COIL_20A.caution: Up to 18 A flows in the coil. Duty (5500A/COIL data): 11 A rms continuous, 20 A rms for 2 minutes then 8 minutes OFF; not confirmed for this coil (UNVERIFIED). Keep the calibrator in STANDBY whenever you touch the coil or leads.
